My private value is $40. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This ensures:
1. I win if the item is worth more to me than others
2. I only pay the second-highest bid
3. I maximize my potential profit
4. Bidding above my value risks losing money
5. Bidding below my value risks not winning when I should

Since this is a single round with no repeated interactions, I'll bid my true value.

Since values are drawn randomly and independently, I'll use a strategic bid that gives me a chance to win while protecting my potential profit margin. I'll bid slightly above my value but not too high. A bid around $14-$15 seems reasonable - it allows me to potentially win if others bid lower, while ensuring I don't overpay relative to my value.

My private value is $17. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing an item worth more to me. If I bid more, I risk paying more than the item's worth to me. Since values are randomly drawn and this is a one-round game, bidding $17 directly represents my best strategic approach to maximize potential profit.
